611 Main is printed on the north frontage between 609 and 615–617, inside the 600 block bracketed by N. 6th and 7th Streets, and in 1918 it carries the Klaus & Thomas Garage (16 cars). A position at x≈68.0%, y≈80.8% was fixed but NOT kept: the only checks available (adjacent house numbers, the 6th/7th block bracket, index range 'Main 401–649, sheet 4') all depend on the same numbering system, so there is no independent held-out feature proving 1918 '611' is the modern Liberty Theater lot. The entry's '1902 hardware building' history is not visible on the sheet either. Upgrade only with an independent check (e.g., a dated building permit or NR nomination naming the 1918 occupant). Morgan's Alley (301–311 Main) is on sheet 3, not sourced.

Placed on the building the sheet itself labels 'UNION DEPOT' at 1233 Main (waiting room centre). Reference points used to fix it: (1) Main St. label and street line; (2) 12th St. at the top of the sheet; (3) the 'Driveway' south of the depot; (4) Camas Prairie R.R. main track; (5) Nez Perce County Court House, labelled across Main; (6) printed house number 1233; (7) block number 224; (8) facing house numbers 1234 and 1302. Held-out checks, not used to fix: (a) the sheet-1 'Specials' index lists 'Union Depot — sheet 11'; (b) the footprint — brick, central waiting room with ticket-office bay toward the track and a baggage room wing — matches the entry's National Register description of the 1909 brick building with waiting spaces and baggage/storage wings. Disagreement: none beyond a street width.

Placed at the centre of the footprint the sheet labels 'ADMINISTRATION BUILDING … being remodeled from fire ruins — from plans' (block 121, 'Lewiston State Normal School'). Reference points: (1) 7th Ave.; (2) 8th Ave.; (3) 9th Ave.; (4) 10th Ave. (not opened); (5) 6th St.; (6) 7th St.; (7) City Park edge; (8) Lewis Hall girls' dormitory and Domestic Science Bldg. labels; (9) Gymnasium label. Held-out: (a) sheet-1 index lists 'Lewiston State Normal School — sheet 26'; (b) the 'fire ruins' note matches the entry's account of the fire that gutted the Normal School. The point marks the Administration Building, not the tower; the sheet does not draw the tower.

The entry's ground is the whole National Register downtown, an area rather than a point. The key map also shows the N.P.R.R. depot at its 1908 site; the entry starts at the depot museum, which was moved from that site, so the 1908 depot position is not the visitor's standing point.
Key map only; the point is on id-wallace-1908-s05.
Area entry (the whole downtown); no single position.

Placed at the centre of the Bank St. × 6th St. intersection as drawn. Reference points: (1) '6TH' street label and the 6th St. right-of-way; (2) Bank St. label (mid-sheet) and its 75-ft right-of-way; (3) 5th St.; (4) 4th St.; (5) corner house numbers 524 (east) and 525 (west) at the 6th St. corner; (6) 520/521 and 518/519 down the block; (7) White & Bender Co. at the north-east corner; (8) printed street width '75''. Held-out: (a) the sheet-1 key map places the 6th St. crossing of Bank at the corner of blocks 19/20/21, where sheet 5 meets sheet 6 — consistent; (b) the sheet-6 reference '6' printed just north of the intersection. The entry says the cover sits slightly off-centre in the roadway; that offset is far less than a street width.

Placed at the centre of the main block of the building printed at 613 Jefferson. Reference points: (1) N. Union St. (west edge of the block); (2) N. Rankin St. (east edge); (3) Jefferson St. label; (4) High St. (north); (5) block number 16; (6) frontage numbers 601, 603, 605, 607, 609, 611, 615, 617, 619 along Jefferson. Held-out, not used to fix: (a) the sheet marks this building '2½' stories with 'B.B.' (brick basement), matching the entry's NRHP 71000444 description of a two-and-a-half-story heavy-timber frame building over a brick basement; (b) the set index assigns Jefferson 601–809 to sheet 10. No disagreement beyond a street width.

Placed at the centre of the main house in block 74. Reference points: (1) Monroe St. (north side of the block); (2) High St. (south side); (3) N. Commerce St. (east); (4) N. Pearl St. (west); (5) block number 74; (6) house numbers 400 and 402 across High St.; (7) the 1st Methodist Church label on block 15; (8) Madison St. at the top of the sheet. Held-out: (a) the set index assigns High 400–517 to sheet 11, and the north frontage of the 400 block of High is block 74, consistent with 401 High St.; (b) the building is drawn as a large two-story brick dwelling standing alone in the block with a central rooftop element marked '3' (read here as the cupola) and an attached rear wing, matching the entry's description of the house with an attached service wing. The sheet prints no name and no house number on the building itself.

The sheet prints 209–215 N. Canal at the Jefferson corner of block 12, with two separate frame dwellings. The entry itself records that the Garden Club and the architectural history give different Canal St. numbers (211 vs. 215), so which drawn building is the house cannot be fixed by address, and the sheet carries no name. Blank by rule.

The sheet shows Broadway, the bluff and the water works but no park boundary; the entry's overlook point at 101 S. Broadway cannot be placed on 1910 ground to street-width accuracy. Under-the-Hill itself is on sheet 25 (not sourced).

Placed at the centre of the footprint the sheet labels 'ST. MARY'S R.C. CATHEDRAL'. Reference points: (1) Main St. (north side of block 31); (2) S. Union St. (west); (3) S. Rankin St. (east); (4) State St. (south); (5) frontage numbers 600, 602, 604, 606 on Main; (6) 101 and 103 on S. Union; (7) the Priest's House and 'Cathedral Park' labels; (8) the Cathedral School across Main. Held-out: (a) the set's Specials index lists 'St. Mary's Cath. and School — sheet 16'; (b) the spire is drawn at the Union St. end and the apse at the east end, consistent with a church fronting Union. The name on the sheet settles the building; the 101/107 address question does not affect the point.

Placed at the centre of the building the sheet labels 'COUNTY COURT HOUSE' in block 14. Reference points: (1) W. Jackson St. (north); (2) W. Grove St. (south); (3) N. Monroe St. (west); (4) N. Cherry St. (east); (5) block number 14; (6) the four W.C. octagons at the square's corners; (7) the County Jail across Grove; (8) St. Mary's Church across Cherry. The entry's note that county offices moved across Cherry St. in 1939 is consistent with the jail block shown across the street.

Placed in the Chartres St. front building of block 43, marked 'Court' and 'District Police Station', at the corner of St. Peter. Reference points: (1) Chartres St.; (2) St. Peter St.; (3) Orleans/Exchange Passage line; (4) Jackson Square (block 24) across Chartres; (5) St. Louis Cathedral (block 45) next door; (6) house numbers 701 and 713 on Chartres; (7) the 'State Arsenal' label in the rear of the block; (8) block number 43. Held-out: (a) the entry's own record places the courts in the Cabildo (the Sala Capitular as the state court's courtroom) and an early police station/guardhouse on this site — matching the sheet's 'Court' and 'Police Station' labels; (b) the Cathedral's index listing ('St. Louis Catholic Cathedral — sheet 121') confirms the sheet.

Placed in the Chartres St. front building of block 46, marked 'Court', at the corner of St. Ann. Reference points: (1) Chartres St.; (2) St. Ann St.; (3) St. Anthony's Alley (St. Anthony St.) separating it from the Cathedral; (4) Royal St.; (5) block number 46; (6) Jackson Square across Chartres; (7) 'Priests House' label inside block 46; (8) Cathedral (block 45). Placed on the 'Jackson Monument' at the centre of the square (block 24); the Cathedral is drawn and labelled directly inland across Chartres in block 45 (centre ≈ x 32.5%, y 52.7%). Reference points: (1) Chartres St.; (2) Decatur St.; (3) St. Peter St.; (4) St. Ann St.; (5) the square's corner fire hydrants; (6) the 'Granite Block' paving notes on both sides; (7) block number 24; (8) the Cathedral label. Placed on the frame dwelling at 628–632 Dumaine (block 47, between Royal and Chartres). Reference points: (1) Dumaine St. label; (2) Royal St.; (3) Chartres St.; (4) St. Ann St.; (5) block number 47; (6) printed Dumaine numbers 600, 610, 612, 618, 622, 624, 628, 630, 632; (7) the 'Macaroni Factory' and 'Wood Yard' labels in the block; (8) 'Cobble Stone' paving note on Dumaine. Held-out: (a) the building is drawn as frame (yellow) marked '1½ B.B.' — one and a half stories over a brick basement — matching the entry's description of a raised cottage with a solid brick basement and brick-between-posts upper story; (b) the sheet's '122' reference across Dumaine confirms the next sheet takes the downriver side, consistent with 632 being on this (block 47) side. Point sits at the 632/630 frontage of the building.
District entry (the whole Vieux Carré). This sheet maps one part of it around Jackson Square; an area is not a point.

The entry's anchor is the Interpretive Center at 415 N. Main. The sheet prints 419 at the North St. corner and 405/403/401 toward Hill St., but no 415; the frontage between is one lumber yard. Interpolating a lot would be a guess, so no point. Useful visible features for a caption: the 'Old Mark Twain Homestead' label on Hill St. in the same block, and the Streckfus Line steamboat dock on the river.

The entry's anchor is the Bauvais-Amoureux House, 327 St. Marys Road, south of the old town. The 1929 Sanborn set (LOC sanborn04855_004) was checked and does not reach St. Mary's Road, so the USGS quadrangle is the sheet that maps this ground. At 1:62,500 the road south of town shows building dots that cannot be identified with the house to street-width accuracy. Blank by rule.

The inset prints the junction of St. Catherine St., Washington Road (now D'Evereux Dr.) and Liberty Road, and the set index lists Liberty Road on sheet 21. The entry is the site of a slave market that left no building on this 1910 sheet. A point on the junction would mark a street corner, not the market, and the sheet gives no footprint for the market. No point.

Placed at the centre of the main block of the brick dwelling beside the printed number 215 on S. Pearl St., in block 38 at the corner of Washington St. Reference points: (1) S. Pearl St. label (west); (2) Washington St. label (south); (3) S. Commerce St. label (east); (4) State St. (north); (5) block number 38; (6) S. Pearl frontage numbers 201–215 running south to the corner; (7) Washington frontage numbers 401–411 below the block; (8) St. Joseph's School and Sisters' Residence labels in the north half of the block. Held-out checks, not used to fix the point: (a) the entry describes a brick house, stuccoed to look like brownstone, with an attached service wing; the sheet draws a brick (pink) two-storey dwelling with a two-storey brick wing running back to the north; (b) the entry describes a columned portico on the front; the sheet draws a one-storey frame porch along the S. Pearl St. face. The sheet prints no name on the building. Disagreement: none beyond a street width.

Placed at the centre of the 2½-storey brick dwelling (marked 'D.') on the south side of State St. in block 45, numbered 210 in the upper number series and 212 in the lower one. Reference points: (1) State St. label; (2) S. Canal St. (west end of the block); (3) S. Wall St. (east end); (4) Washington St. (south); (5) block number 45; (6) the printed numbers 210 and 212 over the front; (7) the vacant 210 lot immediately west; (8) the Mississippi Central R.R. Terminal / Passenger Depot west of that lot; (9) the rear dependency numbered 210½. Held-out checks, not used to fix the point: (a) the NPS William Johnson House Cultural Landscape Report says the family sold the west (Lapice) lot to the Eastern Railway in 1906, all but a 10-ft strip next to the house, and that the railway built a freight and passenger depot there by 1910 (its Fig. 2-33 is this 1910 sheet). The sheet shows the depot west of a narrow open lot beside this building. (b) The report says McCallum owned the east lot and shared a wall with Johnson. The sheet shows a second 2½-storey brick house (marked 'Negro Boarding') on the east party wall. (c) The entry describes a three-bay brick front with two dormers; the sheet draws a 2½-storey brick building. The two number series (210/212) are both printed and are not resolved by the sheet; the point rests on the depot and neighbour relationships, not on the number alone. Disagreement: none beyond a street width.

Placed at the centre of the two-storey brick dwelling (marked '2B', 'D.') at the corner of Orleans St. and the foot of S. Broadway. Reference points: (1) Orleans St. label; (2) S. Broadway label; (3) the 'Private Way' along the west side of the lot; (4) the Rosalie Ware Ho. Co. cotton storage directly south; (5) the Natchez Compress & Ware Ho. Co. office and siding to the north; (6) the hydrants marked 'D.H.' at Private Way and at S. Broadway; (7) the scale bar and the '24' match line at the bottom. Held-out checks, not used to fix the point: (a) the entry says a separate brick kitchen with living quarters survives behind the house; the sheet draws a separate two-storey brick 'Servants' building on the same lot; (b) the house has porticoes on front and rear; the sheet draws porches on two opposite faces of the house. The entry's address is 100 Orleans St. The sheet prints no house number or name; the 'Rosalie Ware Ho. Co.' label next door is consistent but was not used as a check. Disagreement: none beyond a street width.

The sheet prints 'Natchez Under the Hill' with Silver and Ferry Streets, and the set index lists Silver St. and the ferry at Natchez Under the Hill on sheet 25. The entry is a bluff-top park and overlook, not a building the sheet draws. No point. A companion no-point tie to sheet 14 is in v2.

The set index assigns N. Washington St. 700–923 to sheet 4. The entry's museum (910 Washington St.) opened in 2012, and its stories (the 1927 flood, the towboat Mississippi IV) are not on a 1913 sheet. No 1913 feature belongs to the entry, so there is no point. The tie records only what stood along this stretch of Washington St. in 1913.

Placed at the centre of the brick front block of the dwelling beside the printed number 1010 (old number 106) on E. 1st St. (First East St.), in block 5. Reference points: (1) N. Cherry St. label (north); (2) N. Adams St. label (south); (3) the E. 1st St. label; (4) block number 5; (5) the printed numbers 1010 (106), 1018 (108), 1020 and 1022 along the same frontage; (6) the facing numbers 1009 and 1011 across the street; (7) Cherry St. numbers 801–807 at the top of the block; (8) block 4 across E. 1st. The sheet draws exactly that: a two-storey brick front block facing E. 1st, with a frame block attached behind it to the west and a frame porch on the street face. Disagreement: none beyond a street width.

Placed at the centre of the 2½-storey brick dwelling (marked 'D.') beside the printed number 820 on St. Louis St., in block 70. Reference points: (1) St. Louis St. label; (2) Bourbon St. (bottom); (3) Dauphine St. (top of block 70); (4) Conti St. (far side of the block); (5) block number 70; (6) the printed numbers 812, 820, 826, 832 and 836 along St. Louis; (7) the hydrant marked 'OLD' across St. Louis; (8) the Bourbon frontage numbers 405–439. Held-out checks, not used to fix the point: (a) the set index assigns St. Louis 800–1040 (even side) to sheet 118; (b) the entry describes a main house with a separate quarters building across a courtyard behind it. The sheet draws a detached three-storey brick building behind the house on the same lot, across an open yard. The entry describes the house as Federal brick; the sheet draws 2½ storeys in brick. Disagreement: none beyond a street width. The 1870s stable is not identified on the sheet.

Placed at the centre of the long brick building the sheet labels 'ARCHBISHOP R.C.' in block 19, set back from Chartres St. Reference points: (1) Chartres St. label; (2) Hospital St. (north); (3) Ursuline St. (south); (4) Decatur St. (east); (5) block number 19; (6) the 'St. Mary's R.C. Church' label; (7) the 'School' and 'Bell Tower' labels; (8) the cobblestone paving notes on Hospital and Ursuline; (9) the Decatur frontage numbers 1101–1141. Held-out checks, not used to fix the point: (a) the entry says the building was the residence of the bishops and archbishops of New Orleans until 1899, with St. Mary's Church (1845) adjoining it as their chapel. The sheet labels the building 'Archbishop R.C.' and draws St. Mary's R.C. Church attached at its north end. (b) The entry gives the convent as about 160 × 48 ft, with two floors and a dormered attic. On the sheet's scale bar (about 5.9 px per ft) the drawn block measures about 134 × 52 ft, marked 2½ storeys. Disagreement: about 26 ft in length, within a street width. The point is on the building's centre, and it does not depend on the length difference.

Morgan's Alley anchor. The entry gives its own address as a range ('301/311 Main Street, listed as 305'). Over that frontage the sheet shows four separate structures: a two-storey brick at 301; a three-storey brick at 303–307; a one-storey frame bicycle repair shop at 309; and a brick building at 311–313. The sheet alone cannot say which of these footprints are the 1905 Vollmer and Scott building, so a point would be a guess. No point. 'The Tribune' is printed across D St. in block 16 in 1918; the entry says the Tribune was an early upstairs occupant, so by 1918 it had moved. The Liberty Theater (611 Main) stays point-less on sheet 4, as in v2.

The set index assigns Main 2021–2254 to sheet 15, which covers the 2100 block of Main (entry address 2102 Main St.). The park and its locomotive came later than this 1918 sheet, and nothing printed here belongs to them. No point.
